sentences.text: Xenovenator is distinguished by a markedly thickened and domed skull roof formed by the frontal bones.
The shape of its cranial dome resembles that of pachycephalosaurids, a case of convergent evolution.
Scientists have suggested that the reinforced cranium may have been used for head-butting contests between individuals.
The specific epithet espinosai honors the Mexican paleontologist Luis Espinosa.
Rivera-Sylva and colleagues interpreted the expansion and fusion of the dome as reflecting ontogenetic change, meaning the skull thickened as the animal grew.
Phylogenetic analysis places Xenovenator in a late-diverging position within Troodontinae.
It belongs to the tribe Troodontini and the family Troodontidae.
Xenovenator is a member of the class Reptilia.
Xenovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous Campanian age.
The Campanian stage spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
One hypothesis attributes the dome to sexual dimorphism, a pattern common in living mammals and birds but rarely documented in non-avian dinosaurs.
Jasinski & Sullivan later reassigned the species X.? robustus to a new genus, Dinevenator, in the same year it was described.
